newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia set to deport 1,026 illegal workers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia set to deport 1,026 illegal workers.

text.p: Malaysia prepared on Friday to deport 1,026 illegal Indonesian workers, the first of such repatriations after an amnesty for illegal workers expired earlier this week.
The revised figure of just over 1,000 deportees was provided by Malaysian officials supervising the forced exodus at a port here in southern Johor state.
On Thursday, the national Bernama news agency said about 2,000 Indonesians were due to be sent back on an Indonesian naval ship, the Tanjung Osina.
Convoys of police trucks and buses have been transporting illegal workers to the port since Thursday from eight camps and two prisons around Malaysia, the New Straits Times reported on Friday.
The ship is expected to depart from the port at 3 p.m. local time (0700 GMT) on Friday.
The joint Malaysian-Indonesian operation is being carried out after a three-month amnesty period for some one million illegal workers to register with the government ended on December 31, 1996.

An estimated 700,000 workers or 70 percent of the illegal foreign workforce failed to meet the deadline, and are expected to be deported under a massive nationwide operation to hunt down and catch illegal workers.
Labour-short Malaysia, with a population of 20 million, has about two million migrant workers.
